summary: The one Flask application every other feature runs inside: it sets response headers on every response, enforces the CSRF header ahead of authentication, issues and reads the session cookie, opens the SQLite database, and renders the authenticated chrome (top bar, nav, lock button) each screen sits inside.

read.role: the chrome this feature renders — top bar, nav, lock and Update-values buttons; no screen of its own

csp.value: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; connect-src 'self'; img-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'

noXFrameOptions.value: no separate X-Frame-Options header is served; frame-ancestors 'none' in the CSP is the only framing control

hsts.value: includeSubDomains always; preload only once the deployment is internet-reachable on a fixed domain that has served the header stably for the required probation period, not applicable to a LAN/VPN-only deployment

csrfHeader.value: X-Solvent-Request: 1, required on every route not in the exempt list

csrfOrdering.value: the header check runs before authentication, so a request missing it gets Forbidden regardless of whether the session is valid, expired, or absent

csrfExemptRule.value: exempt routes are the server-rendered shell pages reached by navigation, each named individually; no JSON endpoint is exempt, GET /api/export included; an exemption is a named route, never a path pattern, so a new endpoint under an existing prefix inherits nothing

sessionCookie.value: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax; carries only a signed opaque session token, no key material

secretKeyStartupRule.value: the app refuses to start when SECRET_KEY is absent or empty rather than generating one; the failure names the variable and prints no key material

csrfHeaderMissing.condition: the required X-Solvent-Request header is absent, checked before authentication (spec/features/app-shell.md#edge-cases)

csrfPresentSessionInvalid.condition: the header is present but the session is missing/expired/invalid (spec/features/app-shell.md#edge-cases)

unknownRoute.condition: a request to a path the app does not serve (spec/features/app-shell.md#edge-cases)

unhandledFailure.condition: never a designed answer; appears only where a test stubs one, and must still carry CSP/HSTS (spec/features/app-shell.md#acceptance-criteria)

fixtures: one route of each response shape — a shell page, a JSON endpoint, an unknown path, and a stubbed handler that raises unhandled — for the header-parity assertion
one route with a valid session, one with an expired session, and one with no session at all, for the CSRF-before-auth indistinguishability assertion
a seeded admin and a seeded non-admin user, for the nav-entries-by-role criterion
a process-launch harness that can start the app with SECRET_KEY unset or empty, and capture the failure output
focus: the header criterion is easy to fake by asserting CSP/HSTS on one happy-path route alone — the spec requires them on a shell page, a JSON endpoint, a 404, and a 500, and a green test that only checks one proves nothing about the others

the CSRF-before-auth criterion is only observable by comparing the missing-header response across valid, expired, and absent sessions and confirming they are byte-identical (status, body, headers) — a test against a single session state cannot show the check precedes authentication

'a shell navigation route loads without the header' must be tested against an actual exempt route, not a JSON endpoint with the check stubbed out — the exemption is per named route, so the test should also confirm a nearby non-exempt route under the same prefix still rejects

the SECRET_KEY-unset criterion needs an actual process start attempt and inspection of the failure output for the variable name and absence of key material, not a unit test of a config-loading function in isolation

'no response body originating in the shell contains vault plaintext' cannot be checked by grepping the shell's own templates alone, since the shell never has plaintext to begin with — the assertion that matters is that no route wired to the shell ever receives decrypted content to render
